component.name: ChessPenguin
component.summary: Chess database: view, enter and analyse PGN games

description.p: ChessPenguin is a native desktop chess database for PGN files. Open annotated books and game collections, browse games with variations and comments, enter your own games and analyse them with any UCI engine such as Stockfish.

ul.li: Library of PGN databases with a searchable, sortable game list
Move tree with nested variations, comments and NAGs
Engine analysis with several lines, best-move arrows and an evaluation bar
Step through engine lines on the board without changing the game
Copy PGN/FEN, save games, undo and redo
Legacy encodings of real-world PGN files are detected

description.p: Rodent gets Rodent IV's characters and 22 famous players, from Morphy to Kasparov, each with its opening books; on macOS too. On Android the lists are richer: dividers, results at a glance, the opening code, colours by kind of database; search finds by the opening code.

Play against Rodent V, a strong engine with a style of play (Linux and Windows, downloaded once). Each engine's strength is on its own scale: Maia 600–2600, Rodent V 800–3000. Offer the engine a draw. Games against the computer are written by themselves into the player's database. On Android too: Maia 600–2600, draw offers and the player's database.

Play against the large Maia model (downloaded once): the strength slider shows her measured strength on the Lichess blitz scale, from 1100 to 2100. Game analysis starts at once with the options chosen before. On Android: moves on the board, your own databases, games against Maia and the opening trainer.

Paste a line from the clipboard into a game: moves or a whole PGN game go where they part from it, with their comments and variations. Play on from any move against Maia, with the moves of the game kept. Learn an opening: replay from memory the moves of both sides up to a chosen move; mistakes are counted and the runs of each line remembered.

Play against the computer: Maia, a neural network trained on human games, plays like a human of the rating you choose, from 600 to 2600, mistakes included. Lichess time controls from 3+0 to 30+20, your own or unlimited; clocks, premoves, take-backs. No engine hints during the game; when her position is hopeless Maia offers to resign. Afterwards the game can be analysed or saved. Maia (21 MB) is downloaded on request. New board setting: always promote to a queen.

Your own comments in a game: press Enter on a move and write right in the notation, after any move of the main line or a variation, or at the start of the game. Put symbols on moves and positions (! ? !! ?? !? ?! and = ∞ ± ∓ …) with the mouse or Ctrl+1…6, draw arrows and circles on the board with the right mouse button. Book comments can be edited; their paragraphs and embedded commands are kept.

Your own databases: create an empty PGN database, add any game to it, save your changes back with Ctrl+S, edit the game data (players, event, date, result, annotator) and delete games with Undo. A new game can be started right in a database with «+ Game». The library's title row holds the actions: new game, paste PGN, add or create a database, online games.
A new icon: a penguin in a crown.
Android: the offer of a new version can be closed and turned back on in Settings; no more links to GitHub in the update screens.
The update check goes through the ChessPenguin site, which counts installations that run: only a random number of the installation, the version and the system are sent.

ChessPenguin 1.0: three more interface languages — Brazilian Portuguese, Uzbek and Kazakh, nine in all. On Android the players stand above and below the board, and both names are shown in full in the list of games.

Narrow windows no longer overlap: the reference tab and the engine settings fit their panel, the filters open over the list and the search board takes its place in a narrow window, and a narrow tall window shows the notation under the board. The window can be made as small as 640×480.
The filter panel keeps its width while a name is typed and its rows are aligned. Escape in a game with unsaved edits asks about saving again.

Every database — PGN files of any size, downloads from Lichess and Chess.com, archives and small ChessBase databases — gets the filters and the position search of a large ChessBase database: players, tournament, years, rating, result, ECO, length, comments, variations, with name suggestions and sorting. A quick search in the header of every database finds each word in any field. Games downloaded from Lichess and Chess.com are shown newest first.

The Android app updates itself: it finds a new release, downloads and checks it, and hands it to Android to install. The release page now lists what is new. The desktop app checks for updates with the same shared code; nothing changes for it otherwise.

The Android app downloads any player's games from Lichess and Chess.com by nickname into a database, lists them from the most recent one, and later fetches only the new games. Its status bar follows the theme chosen in the app.

The Android app gets the game report of the desktop: inaccuracies, mistakes and blunders in the notation, an evaluation graph, each player's accuracy, and the better move of every error on the board. Both apps now share the same report code and give the same numbers.

A game whose tags follow the previous game's result on the same line now shows its players in the games list. The Android app pastes PGN from the clipboard, opens files from other apps, and stays smooth while the engine thinks.

The Android app gets the boards and piece sets of the desktop app, numbers in the games list, an engine that turns on only with its button, and a fix for the engine download that said there was not enough space. The desktop app is unchanged.

In a game, Up goes to the end and Down to the start, Shift+Up/Down switch variations, and Escape goes back to the previous game or the library once nothing else is open. The Android app adds whole folders of databases, ChessBase databases too.
The first alpha of ChessPenguin for Android: databases, games and Stockfish on the phone. The desktop app is unchanged.
The 0.8 series together: the reference tab, games from Lichess and Chess.com, self-update, translated comments, move notation and piece animation; symbols that showed as empty boxes now render.
The side panel no longer widens by itself while comments are translated; comments in variations have the usual size; no scroll bar pops up over the engine lines.
Translation with a ChatGPT subscription works; short comments and text in brackets are translated too.

Comments in another language are translated into yours — with a ChatGPT Plus or Pro subscription, an API key, or a model on this computer; moves are never changed and nothing is written to the PGN. Moves can be shown as figurines or in the letters of your language. Pieces slide on the board, as on Lichess.

Starts on more machines: when the graphics do not cooperate, other ways of drawing are tried and the one that works is kept; a start that still fails says why. The online games window opens with an empty nickname.
The side panel fits small screens: on a laptop screen the reference tab no longer slides under the board.

Games from Lichess and Chess.com: download anyone's games by nickname — yours, a pupil's, an opponent's — into a database, both sites merged or one per site, and fetch the new ones with one click. Interrupted downloads continue without duplicates.

Updates: ChessPenguin tells when a new version is out and updates itself where it can (Windows, AppImage, the Linux archive); for packages it downloads the new one and shows the command that installs it.

The «Reference» tab of a game: what was played in the current position in a database of the shelf — the moves with their statistics and the strongest games, the novelty of the game, and its copy in the database. The board always keeps the full height of the window.

Faster position search in large ChessBase databases: an opening index (when there is enough memory) and a search index of its own for databases without one. Quieter import notes; the email in Settings → About is copied on click.
Settings → About: the version, links to the website, the release notes and the source code, and the support contacts.
Sample databases at the first start (38 classic games, 267 games of Alekhine); the first start uses the system language.
Stockfish is downloaded on request (smaller packages; the Flatpak keeps it inside); macOS builds for Apple Silicon; position search fixes and narrow-window layout.

Find games by position: play moves on a board next to the game list and see the games that reach the position by any move order, with the moves played next and their results; works with the filters, in books also in variations.
Large ChessBase databases (Mega Database, millions of games) open in seconds, with a filter panel: player with suggestions, opponent, tournament, years, Elo, result, ECO, moves, annotations.
Opens ChessBase databases (.cbh, .cbv) and zip/7z archives; move badges and refutation arrows; viewed games marked; more piece sets, boards and sounds.
Game analysis with accuracy, mistakes and an evaluation graph; Stockfish 19 included.
First public release.
